overunder.label: Over/unders
overunder.hint: alternating either side of a target

workouts.name: 20-Minute FTP Test
workouts.purpose: Start the 20 minutes just above your current FTP and settle into the hardest power you can hold evenly for the whole effort — no fading in the last five. FTP is estimated as 95% of your 20-minute average.

workouts.name: Ramp Test
workouts.purpose: Ride each step in ERG until you can no longer hold it. The app ends the ramp when your power falls away and drops you into a cool-down. FTP is estimated as 75% of your best one-minute average. The steps scale from your current FTP, so if that number is badly out, set a rough guess first.

workouts.name: The Long Glass
workouts.recommended: A first ride. Half an hour at 69% — long enough to feel like training, short enough that nothing can go wrong.

workouts.name: Flatwater
workouts.recommended: The Z2 hour. If you only ever did one workout on repeat, this is the one.

workouts.name: The Causeway
workouts.recommended: The long ride, for when there’s time. Same intensity as Flatwater, just more of it.

workouts.name: Stonemason
workouts.recommended: Tempo done properly: long steady blocks, honest but not hard. The step between Z2 and sweet spot.

workouts.name: Brazier
workouts.recommended: The classic 15-minute sweet spot blocks — the most time-efficient FTP builder in the library.

workouts.name: Sunstroke
workouts.recommended: Sweet spot with volume. The session that moves FTP once the 60-minute version stops being hard.

workouts.name: Fault Line
workouts.recommended: Threshold at threshold: 8-minute efforts at exactly FTP. The workout that tells you whether your number is right.

workouts.name: Endline
workouts.recommended: The race-shaped one: alternating just under and just over threshold. Teaches you to recover while still working.

workouts.name: Coldlash
workouts.recommended: The gentler way into VO₂ work: thirty seconds on, thirty off. More time at high oxygen uptake than the 4×4, with less suffering per rep.

workouts.name: Live Wire
workouts.recommended: The only anaerobic session most people need. Short, sharp, done in 45.

workouts.name: Norwegian 4×4
workouts.purpose: Governed by heart rate, not power: aim to reach 90–95% of your max HR by the end of each rep, climbing into it rather than starting there. 110% FTP gets most riders there. If HR isn’t at 90% by the end of rep 2, nudge the intensity up; if rep 4 is unfinishable, start lower next time. Keep pedalling through the recoveries — they’re deliberately short.

blocks.label: Easy
blocks.cue: Easy spinning. Let the legs wake up — nothing to prove yet.

blocks.label: Building
blocks.cue: Lift the cadence a touch. Breathing should still be easy.

blocks.label: Warm-up
blocks.cue: Last easy minutes. Find the cadence you’ll use for the reps — 90+ suits most people.

blocks.label: Opener
blocks.cue: One minute to open the legs. This isn’t a rep — don’t chase it.

blocks.label: Settle
blocks.cue: Ease right off and let the heart rate drop. Rep 1 starts fresh.

work.label: VO₂
cue: Settle into it. Heart rate climbs slowly — aim for about 90% of max by the end, not the start.
Same power. HR should reach 90%+ by the end of this one. If it isn’t close, nudge the intensity up 2–3%.
The hardest one. Hold the number and let HR sit in the 90–95% band.
Last rep — empty it. HR 92–95% in the final minute. If you can’t finish, start lower next time.

rest.label: Recovery
cue: Keep pedalling, easy. HR won’t come all the way down — that’s the design.
One to go. Keep the legs moving.

blocks.label: Cool-down
blocks.cue: Ease down. Let the heart rate drift back under 70% of max.

workouts.recommended: The VO₂max session with the research behind it: four 4-minute efforts you can actually finish, with your heart rate doing the coaching.
